title: Fermiology of the kagome compound LuNb6Sn6 probed by de Haas-van Alphen oscillations
authors: Tucker Beekmann, Caue Kaufmann Ribeiro, Kyryl Shtefiienko, Jiaqiang Yan, Brenden R. Ortiz, Christopher A. Mizzi, Keshav Shrestha
abstract: We report a detailed de Haas-van Alphen (dHvA) study of the recently discovered kagome metal LuNb6Sn6 using torque magnetometry, magnetization, and heat-capacity measurements. Temperature-dependent torque and heat-capacity data reveal a charge density wave (CDW) transition at T_CDW = 85 K. The thermal hysteresis observed in both measurements establishes the first-order nature of the transition. Quantum oscillation measurements identify two major dHvA frequencies: F_alpha ~ 20 T and F_beta ~ 200 T, and their angular dependence is consistent with ellipsoidal Fermi surface (FS) pockets. Landau fan diagram analysis reveals evidence for a nontrivial Berry phase associated with the F_alpha pocket, indicating possible nontrivial electronic topology in LuNb6Sn6. Analysis of the temperature and magnetic field dependence of the oscillations using the Lifshitz-Kosevich formula yields electronic parameters that indicate anisotropic quantum transport properties. First-principles calculations provide further insight into the electronic structure, revealing Dirac-like band crossings, a flat band, and multiple van Hove singularities near the Fermi level. Our calculations based on the pristine phase cannot fully reproduce the experimentally observed quantum oscillation frequencies, suggesting that CDW-induced FS reconstruction plays a crucial role in the ground-state electronic structure of LuNb6Sn6. These results provide new insight into the FS topology and electronic structure of LuNb6Sn6, enriching our understanding of the electronic properties of kagome materials.
summary: This work uses de Haas-van Alphen oscillations and thermal measurements on the kagome metal LuNb6Sn6 to map its Fermi surface topology. The research reveals two distinct electronic pockets whose behavior is significantly altered by a first-order Charge Density Wave transition. By combining quantum oscillation data with DFT calculations, the authors establish that CDW reconstruction dictates the material's ground state electronic structure.
main_problem: To investigate the Fermi surface topology and electronic structure of the kagome metal LuNb6Sn6, particularly in relation to its Charge Density Wave (CDW) transition.
main_result: The study confirms two major quantum oscillation frequencies ($F_\alpha$ and $F_ eta$) originating from ellipsoidal Fermi pockets, while also showing that CDW-induced Fermi surface reconstruction is crucial for understanding the ground state electronic structure.
method: A combination of experimental measurements (dHvA oscillations via torque magnetometry, heat capacity) and theoretical calculations (DFT band structure analysis) was employed.
model_or_system: The physical system is the kagome compound LuNb6Sn6. The investigation focuses on its electronic properties near the Fermi level, particularly how these are modified by a temperature-dependent CDW transition.
key_observables: dHvA frequencies ($F_\alpha \approx 20	ext{ T}, F_ eta \approx 200	ext{ T}$), CDW transition temperatures ($	ext{T}_{	ext{CDW}} = 85	ext{ K}$), and the angular dependence of quantum oscillation frequencies.
important_parameters: Low temperature (2 K), magnetic fields up to 14 T, and electronic parameters derived from Lifshitz-Kosevich analysis ($m^*$, $T_D$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the observed quantum oscillations are governed by well-defined Fermi surface pockets whose topology can be mapped using standard solid-state physics models (e.g., ellipsoidal FS).
figures_summary: Figures show thermal anomalies confirming a first-order CDW transition, dHvA oscillations in torque vs. H, FFT spectra identifying two main frequencies, and plots showing the angle dependence of these frequencies consistent with ellipsoidal pockets.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the material's phase transitions (CDW) using thermal measurements, followed by detailed quantum oscillation measurements to map the Fermi surface topology, and finally comparing experimental findings against first-principles electronic structure calculations.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism/transport, the interplay between symmetry breaking (CDW formation) and the resulting changes in electronic band structure and topological features (Berry phase evidence) is highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phases in strongly correlated systems.

FIG. 2. (a) Torque τ as a function of magnetic field H for a LuNb6Sn6 single crystal (Sample S1) measured at 2 K with the field applied at an angle θ = 45◦. τ(H) exhibits clear dHvA oscillations above 2 T. The black, dashed line represents a second-order polynomial fit to the background. Inset: schematic illustration of the tilt angle and background-subtracted torque signal showing the dHvA oscillations. (b) FFT spectrum of the oscillatory signal shown in (a). Two dominant frequencies are observed at Fα = 12.8 T and Fβ = 259 T.

FIG. 3. (a) Background-subtracted angle-dependent torque data for a LuNb6Sn6 single crystal (Sample S1) at 2 K. dHvA oscillations are observed for all tilt angles. (b) Frequency spectra in the low-frequency range with FFT analysis performed between 2–14 T. (c) Frequency spectra in the high-frequency range with FFT analysis performed between 8–14 T. In both (b) and (c) FFT amplitudes have been normalized by the maximum peak amplitude and offset by a constant to emphasize the angular dependence. Frequencies marked with an asterisk are the focus of the quantitative analysis.

FIG. 4. Angle dependence of (a) Fα and (b) Fβ for LuNb6Sn6 (Sample S1). Solid circles represent data obtained from torque measurements and open circles are symmetrized data. Gray stars correspond to VSM measurements. The solid curves in both panels represent the frequency–angle relation expected for an ellipsoidal FS, indicating that both Fα and Fβ originate from ellipsoidal Fermi pockets. The dashed lines are expected frequency-angle relations for spherical or cylindrical FS. The values and uncertainties of the frequencies in both panels are from fitting a pseudo-Voigt function for each peak. All data acquired at T = 2 K.

FIG. 5. (a) Background-subtracted magnetization as a function of inverse magnetic field with H ∥ab for three LuNb6Sn6 samples (S1, S2, and S3) measured at 2 K. (b) In all three samples, FFTs of the background-subtracted magnetization reveal two main quantum oscillation frequencies near Fα ≈19 T and Fβ ≈204 T, emphasizing the reproducibility of the results. The magnetization data and FFTs have been offset by constants for visual clarity.
